newsitem.title: UK: Railtrack, EWS agree freight deal.
newsitem.headline: Railtrack, EWS agree freight deal.

text.p: British railway infrastructure operator Railtrack Plc said on Friday it had reached outline agreement with American-owned English Welsh and Scottish Railway (EWS), the country's largest bulk freight and parcel operator, on a four-year track access and market development pact.
"The deal has been struck after several months of negotiations and is now being formalised by lawyers before being submitted to the Rail Regulator for ratification," Railtrack said in a statement.
EWS accounts for some 80 percent of its freight income and the deal would underwrite much of this, the company added.

EWS is partly-owned by Wisconsin Central Transportation Corp, one of the largest pure freight operators in the U.S., which in 1995 and 1996 bought stakes in Britain's three main bulk freight companies as well as the national mail and parcel distribution company which includes among its activities operation of the Queen's royal train.
Other investors in its consortium include New Zealand bank Fay, Richwhite & Co and Boston institution Berkshire Partners.

A Railtrack spokesman said that the deal as agreed would address track access charges as well as infrastructure-related issues, including the politically-charged ambition of ensuring more freight is transported on Britain's privatised railways.
Full details of the deal would only be made public when the regulator has assessed it and given it the all-clear, he added.
Railtrack shares firmed in an active but otherwise weak stock market on Friday, even before the freight announcement.
By 1055 the shares were up 5-1/2 pence at 389 pence.
Analysts said the main impetus behind the move was the prospect of the company making cost savings via a new plan to reorganise some of its maintenance units.
